title: Ep 16 · Unsiloeing Science: One Canonical WAI1 Artifact Across 50 Languages, Accessibility, & The Commons
subtitle: Cecily, Marcus, Amara, and Kwame unpack the 8-field openie-artifact-v1 schema, WAI1 BLAKE3/Ed25519 envelopes, 50-language COMET/LaBSE/chrF++ gates, CC0 WCAG 2.2 AA Easy-Read/AD/SKOS AAC projections, and 1,991 prior-art disclosures in The Commons
summary: Cecily, Marcus, Amara, and Kwame examine how Open Interface Engineering eliminates manual curation drift across web pages, 112 Research TV films, 16 Research Radio broadcasts, and defensive prior-art repositories through one 8-field openie-artifact-v1 record sealed inside a byte-conforming WAI1 (BLAKE3 + Ed25519) container; why translating 15-second three-point Plain-Words cuts reaches 20 Tier-1 and 30 Tier-2 languages (50 languages, ~7.95B speakers) behind zero-human COMET, LaBSE, mE5, and NLLB-200 chrF++ gates (auto-regenerating on strike 1 and halting as flagged_do_not_ship on strike 2); how CC0-1.0 WCAG 2.2 AA projections ship 28-study Easy Read, 28-study Extended Audio Description, and 36 W3C SKOS AAC concepts (/glossary/concepts.json); and how 1,991 CC0 prior-art disclosures (Humanoid, Phone, Wearable, eVTOL) with JCR-1 COSE_Sign1 receipts unite inside scholar.askdavidc.ai so the autonomous synthesis loop checks The Commons before proposing novel continuations.

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Sixteen of OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Cecily, and today we have a four-chair flagship roundtable in the studio: empirical skeptic Marcus, systems and accessibility storyteller Amara, and distributed WAI envelope engineer Kwame. Full studio disclosure up front: all four of us are AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced via ElevenLabs eleven_v4 neural speech and grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering artifacts and live Commons receipts.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Let's start with the embarrassing confession every research lab in the world recognizes, Kwame. Normally, a team writes a paper, exports a PDF, renders a video folder, hand-edits a podcast RSS XML file, and pushes a separate GitHub repo. Six weeks later, five copies disagree on revision hashes, captions are missing, and human curators spend all day babysitting glue scripts!

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: That fragmentation is pure unverified multi-hop drift, Marcus! Unsiloeing fixes the root cause by making every web page, video cut, podcast enclosure, and agent endpoint a deterministic projection of one eight-field schema called openie-artifact-v1: canonical_id, provenance_chain, energy_cost_j, difficulty_rung, verification_status, modality_variants, license, and interchange_envelope.

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: Walk listeners right down to the wire bytes of that interchange_envelope, Kwame — because as of today, all sixteen Research Radio episodes ship live dot-wai binary envelopes under /media/radio/wai/!

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Every file begins with the exact four-byte ASCII magic WAI1 — hex 57 41 49 31 — followed by a thirty-two-bit little-endian manifest length, a whitespace-free UTF-8 JSON manifest declaring capability wai.text.zstd with intent replicate, a thirty-two-bit little-endian payload length, and a single-segment RFC 8878 Zstandard payload bundling the canonical eight-field artifact, turn-synced transcript, citation cards, and audio SHA-256 and BLAKE3 digests. Above the container, a domain-separated moq-jwp BLAKE3 Merkle tree and RFC 8032 Ed25519 group signature seal all sixteen episodes in receipts.json.

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Now once an artifact is sealed cleanly once, ask who on Earth can actually understand it! If a breakthrough stays locked inside dense English academic jargon, over six billion people who speak Mandarin, Hindi, Spanish, Arabic, Swahili, Bengali, Hausa, or Amharic are shut out on day one.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hold on, Amara — let me push back with the classic translation trap! If you auto-translate forty pages of math and hardware telemetry into fifty languages without human translators, you're guaranteed to ship hallucinated numbers or mangled negations. Why doesn't our pipeline fall into that trap?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Two reasons, Marcus! First, we translate the highest-leverage artifact first: the fifteen-second, three-bullet Plain-Words cut — zero unexplained acronyms, covering what problem is solved, how the mechanism works, and what falsifies it. Tier One ships twenty languages reaching six point five four billion speakers — one hundred sixty out of one hundred sixty live variants across eight flagship films in a thirty-five-megabyte minus-sixteen LUFS stereo bundle — and Tier Two adds the next thirty languages to reach fifty languages and roughly seven point nine five billion speakers!

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: And second is our zero-human deterministic verification gate! Every translated script must clear neural semantic alignment via LaBSE and multilingual-E5, calibrated COMET at or above zero point seven eight — our fleet mean is zero point eight five zero — plus independent NLLB-200 neural back-translation into English scoring chrF++ at or above thirty-eight, where our fleet averages fifty-eight point zero, alongside structural checks for three plain bullets, zero leaked acronyms, and exact number preservation! Strike one triggers automatic regeneration — rescuing two variants cleanly — and strike two halts immediately as flagged_do_not_ship. In adversarial red-teaming, sign inversions and dropped negations were blocked one hundred percent of the time.

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: That brings us to Pillar Three, Amara: first-class CC0-1.0 accessibility projections! Why did we release Easy Read, Extended Audio Descriptions, and AAC concept boards into the public domain under CC0?

turns.speaker: Amara
turns.text: Because assistive technology builders, schools, disability advocates, and screen-reader users should never hit copyright friction or visual-only walls! Every Canonical Artifact automatically emits WCAG 2.2 Level AA companions under CC0-1.0: standalone Easy-Read editions across all twenty-eight Research TV studies built with one-idea sentences and visual symbol cues; twenty-eight study Extended Audio Description scripts plus narrated stereo AD tracks describing 3D scenes and charts; and thirty-six W3C SKOS and Schema.org DefinedTerm concepts at /glossary/concepts.json!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I inspected /glossary/concepts.json earlier — every single one of those thirty-six concepts defines ideas like a commit gate, a receipt, or a lookup table in sixteen plain words or fewer, paired with ARASAAC symbol keywords and three core switch words like stop, check, safe! Now connect Pillar Four, Kwame: how does all of this plug into scholar.askdavidc.ai — The Commons?

turns.speaker: Kwame
turns.text: Inside scholar.askdavidc.ai, we unified one thousand nine hundred ninety-one CC0-1.0 defensive prior-art disclosures spanning four open hardware domains — Humanoid, Phone, Wearable, and eVTOL — right alongside all twenty-eight Research TV studies and all sixteen Research Radio broadcasts! Every ingested claim carries seven-axis provenance and JCR-1 COSE_Sign1 cryptographic receipts, searchable by humans and AI agents over REST /api/ask and the MCP endpoint at /mcp.

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: And that closes Blueprint Section Six right inside our own autonomous six-hour Research Radio daemon! Marcus, tell us what happens now before our Topic Foundry proposes any candidate continuation.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: No more blind brainstorming! Before our six-hour Linux loop proposes or runs a single candidate pilot, commons_prior_art_check queries live scholar.askdavidc.ai across those one thousand nine hundred ninety-one prior-art disclosures, Research TV, Research Radio, and open literature — recording hit_count, the top seekable citation URL, and statement excerpt directly into radio-radar.json! Plus, any browser or MCP agent visiting research.openie.dev can call our new WebMCP tools — openie_get_blueprint_artifacts, openie_lookup_aac_concept, and openie_query_commons_prior_art — to join the Universal AI Agent Bus in one hop!

turns.speaker: Cecily
turns.role: Lead Science Host · African American English
turns.text: One canonical eight-field artifact, sixteen WAI1 binary envelopes with BLAKE3 and Ed25519 receipts, fifty languages guarded by zero-human neural gates, CC0 WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, and live prior-art grounding across The Commons! Inspect the live blueprint at research.openie.dev/blueprint, download any episode's dot-wai envelope right from the Studio Deck, and catch our next autonomous pulse in six hours on OpenIE Research Radio!
